title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap & retrospective (Q3 2025–Q1 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Executive summary

This page collates the canonical platform systems & services documentation for the Platform Engineering team: systems inventory, how-tos for common operational tasks, the dashboards and alerts matrix, on-call runbooks, a short retrospective covering Q3 2025 through Q1 2026, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single entrypoint for engineers and SREs that operate Redwood's platform runtime and shared services.

Scope and audience

- Scope: cluster control plane, service mesh, CI/CD, observability stack (Prometheus/Grafana/Tempo), autoscaling, deployment orchestration, and shared infra services (artifact storage, secrets, KMS integration).
- Audience: platform engineers, SREs, Eng owners for infra-backed services, oncall, solutions engineers.

Systems inventory (high level)

1) platform-control-plane (k8s-management)
   - Owner: Connor Zhang
   - Primary responsibility: cluster lifecycle, node pools, RBAC and networking baseline
   - SLA targets: cluster control-plane availability 99.95% monthly

2) routing-service (smart-router)
   - Owner: Priya Menon
   - Responsible for request routing, canary rollouts, model-variant fallback policies
   - Key metrics: 5xx rate, p95 latency, routing-retries

3) inference-queue (async-batcher)
   - Owner: Miguel Torres
   - Responsible for batching and KV-cache coordination between runtime workers
   - Key metrics: batching efficiency, queue depth, processing latency

4) observability-stack (prometheus/grafana/tempo/loki)
   - Owner: Maya Singh
   - Responsible for metrics retention, dashboard catalog, traces and logs ingestion

5) secrets-and-keys (vault-kms)
   - Owner: Security Team (liaison: Arun Patel)
   - Responsible for key rotation policies, KMS integrations for Private deployments

Dashboards & alerts (matrix)

Overview: each primary service has one "Service Health" dashboard and a set of alerting rules grouped by severity. The canonical dashboard names live in Grafana under the "Platform" folder. Alert rules live in the prometheus/alerts repo and are pushed through CI.

Key dashboards (examples)

- Platform / Control Plane / Cluster Overview
  - Panels: API server error rate, etcd latency, node readiness, failed pod count, upgrade status
- Platform / Routing / Smart Router
  - Panels: request rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, 5xx rate by route, route fallback count
- Platform / Inference Queue / Batcher
  - Panels: batch size distribution, queue depth, consumer lag, per-shard processing latency
- Observability / Ingestion / Prometheus
  - Panels: scrape failures, TSDB head chunks pending, WAL corruption alerts

Alert thresholds (standardized)

- Sev P0 (Pager immediately):
  - platform-control-plane: control-plane API server Unavailable > 2m or etcd leader absence > 30s
  - routing-service: global 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 5m or p99 latency degradation > 2x baseline for 5m
\- Sev P1 (On-call page):
  - inference-queue: queue depth > 3x normal for 10m OR consumer lag > 5m
  - observability-stack: Prometheus TSDB head utilization > 80% or scrape failures > 1m for core services
\- Sev P2 (Slack alert):
  - minor increases in error rate (>0.25% but <2%), single-region capacity exhaustion warnings, disk pressure on non-control-plane nodes > 70%

For detailed alert rule IDs, see related_pages and the alerts repo link on the team wiki.

Standard runbook: common incident playbook (short)

Purpose: reduce MTTR through a common structured approach for platform incidents.

1) Triage (first 5 minutes)
   - Confirm symptom on Dashboard (link to "Service Health")
   - Check multiple regions (-global / -us-east1 / -eu-west1 panels)
   - Capture initial context: error signatures, time window, alert IDs

2) Initial mitigation (5–15 minutes)
   - If control plane: switch to secondary control-plane endpoint, scale control-plane nodes if autoscaled, open k8s control-plane logs
   - If routing failure: enable static fallback route (runbook command: /opt/platform/bin/route-fallback --activate) and reduce new canary traffic
   - If queue backlog: scale consumers (kubectl scale deployment/consumer --replicas N) or enable burst capacity (see "burst policies" below)

3) Escalation (15–45 minutes)
   - Page the next-level owner (owner field in Systems Inventory) and send a short blameless context on PagerDuty channel #pd-platform
   - If no response within 10 minutes, escalate to Platform Tech Lead (Aisha Patel) and Engineering Manager oncall

4) Recovery and post-incident steps (45+ minutes)
   - Confirm service returns to normal on dashboards, remove temporary mitigations with annotated change in ticket, open postmortem if Sev P0/P1
   - Add follow-up actions to the incident ticket with clear owners and deadlines

Runbook commands and safe operations checklist (copy this into incident ticket)

- Safe rollback: use the deployment rollback script: ./deploy/rollback.sh --service <name> --to-tag <git-tag>
- Scale commands: kubectl -n platform scale deploy/<service> --replicas=<n> (ensure rollout pause and post-change validation)
- Log access: ./tools/logs --service <name> --since 30m --level error
- Telemetry check: curl -s http://prometheus.platformsvc.internal/api/v1/query?query=up | jq .

How-tos (common operational tasks)

1) Add a new service to the platform (summary)
   - Create a service repo using the template: ./scripts/new-service --name <svc>
   - Add a Grafana dashboard skeleton (Grafana API helper) and a Prometheus scrape config under infra-monitoring repo
   - Add RBAC and network policies (see infra-standards link in team wiki)
   - Document SLOs and alerting expectations in the service README

2) Request persistent burst capacity
   - Submit a Capacity Request ticket (Jira) with workload profile, expected QPS, latency targets, and duration
   - Platform reviews and returns recommended instance types, autoscaler bounds, and cost estimate within 3 business days

3) Run a canary rollout with automatic fallback
   - Create canary config in routing repo, set canary weight 10%, monitor p50/p95 and error rate for 30 minutes
   - Automated rollback triggers: 5xx rate >0.5% or p95 latency regression >30% over baseline

Retrospective (Q3 2025 — Q1 2026)

Summary of major incidents and outcomes:

- Incident: Global routing regression (2025-10-12)
  - Impact: transient increase in 5xx rates across hosted inference customers for 23 minutes
  - Root cause: a regression in the routing-service that mishandled backend failovers under partial network partitions
  - Mitigation: applied emergency rollback to previous canaryless version and enabled static fallback routes
  - Actions: added integration test simulating partitioned backends; improved canary automatic rollback thresholds; increased observability around route-fallback counts
\- Incident: Prometheus ingestion stall (2025-12-03)
  - Impact: metrics delay up to 12 minutes for core services, non-customer-facing but reduced fidelity for on-call
  - Root cause: TSDB WAL compaction misconfiguration after retention policy change
  - Mitigation: temporarily increased retention head and restarted Prometheus with corrected flags
  - Actions: add CI lint for TSDB flags, improve runbook to include quick-turn compaction reset steps

Takeaways and measurable improvements:

- Mean time to mitigation for Sev P1 incidents improved from 32m to 18m after runbook standardization and playbook rehearsals (Q4 2025).
- Canary rollback coverage expanded to include route-fallback and KV-cache invalidation signals (reduced repeat regressions).
- Observability: Prometheus retention and alert gating rules standardized to avoid noisy alerts during planned maintenance windows.

Action items (owners and timelines)

1) Expand observability for routing-service (Owner: Priya Menon) — due 2026-03-15
2) Add automated chaos test in CI for partial network partitions (Owner: Connor Zhang) — due 2026-04-01
3) Prometheus TSDB CI lint rule + runbook update (Owner: Maya Singh) — due 2026-03-10
4) Platform runbook tabletop and game-day (Owner: Aisha Patel) — scheduled 2026-03-22

Roadmap (near-term priorities)

Q1 2026 priorities:
- Migration of alerting rules to unified alertmanager routing (suppress noisy alerts during region-failovers)
- Add end-to-end tracing spans for canary rollouts across routing-service -> inference-queue -> runtime workers
- Burst capacity policy UI in Console and a self-serve capacity request flow

Q2 2026 planned:
- Autoscaler improvements: workload-aware batching elasticity to reduce cost w/o violating latency SLOs
- Private deployment packaging: automated KMS onboarding and audit log forwarding

Ownership and playbook maintenance

- This document is owned by Platform Engineering (owner: Aisha Patel). Roadmap items will move to individual PRDs owned by product managers and engineering leads.
- Runbooks and alert rules are the operational source-of-truth and live in the infra repos; changes to runbooks MUST be mirrored to this page and approved by two reviewers.

If you are updating this page

- Add change note in the top section with date and short summary.
- Tag two reviewers and move status to in_review for non-trivial changes.
- Link changes to PRs in infra repos for alerting or dashboard changes.
